digest.headline: The US Federal Reserve raised interest rates as central banks across the globe adjusted monetary policy and energy disruptions hit markets.

lede.b: The Federal Reserve, which is the central bank of the United States that sets monetary policy and regulates financial institutions, raised interest rates for the first time since 2023 on September 17, 2026. This means the central bank made borrowing more expensive in order to cool down the economy. Goldman Sachs called for an October hike because they are worried about rising inflation, which is the general increase in prices over time. Meanwhile, the Nasdaq stock index climbed higher following the rate decision. President Trump claimed the central bank tightened rates for political reasons.
lede.i: The Federal Reserve raised interest rates for the first time since 2023 on September 17, 2026, prompting Goldman Sachs to call for an October hike due to renewed inflation risks. This tightening cycle triggered political friction as President Trump claimed the central bank acted for political reasons. Equity markets absorbed the move differently, with the Nasdaq climbing following the policy announcement. Globaltech simultaneously pursued a Nasdaq uplisting after completing a reverse stock split, though the exchange has not yet approved the application.
lede.a: The Federal Reserve executed its first rate hike since 2023 on September 17, 2026, drawing political criticism from President Trump over alleged motivations. Goldman Sachs responded by issuing a call for an October hike, citing renewed inflation pressures. Risk assets proved resilient initially as the Nasdaq climbed through the session. Concurrently, Globaltech sought a Nasdaq uplisting following a 1-for-3 reverse split, though regulatory approval remains pending due to unmet listing requirements.

thread.b: Central banks in the United States, United Kingdom, Japan, and Brazil adjusted their monetary policies and interest rates. At the same time, Saudi Aramco halted oil supplies to Indian refiners after a pipeline was hit during a Gulf crisis. Energy costs and commodity prices continued to influence global markets.
thread.i: Central bank actions dominated global markets as the US Federal Reserve hiked rates, the Bank of England held steady, and the Bank of Japan lifted its benchmark rate to 1.25%. Concurrently, physical supply shocks rippled through energy markets as Saudi Aramco halted crude shipments to Indian refiners following pipeline damage in the Gulf.
thread.a: Monetary authorities recalibrated policy settings globally, highlighted by the Federal Reserve's rate hike, the Bank of England's hold at 3.75%, and the Bank of Japan's move to 1.25%. Concurrently, physical supply constraints materialized in energy markets as Saudi Aramco halted crude flows to Indian refiners following a pipeline strike amid the Gulf crisis.

United States of America.label: United States
United States of America.sub: Federal Reserve raises rates as markets react

stories.t: Federal Reserve Raises Interest Rates
stories.b: The Federal Reserve, which is the central bank of the United States and sets the cost of borrowing money, raised interest rates for the first time since 2023. President Trump claimed the central bank is raising rates for political reasons. Goldman Sachs called for an October hike, which underscores renewed tightening risks. The Nasdaq climbed after the rate hike decision on September 17, 2026.
stories.i: The Federal Reserve raised interest rates for the first time since 2023. President Trump claimed the central bank is tightening for political reasons. Goldman Sachs issued a call for an October hike, underscoring renewed inflation risks. The Nasdaq climbed following the rate decision on September 17, 2026.
stories.a: The Federal Reserve executed its first rate hike since 2023, drawing claims of political motivation from President Trump. Goldman Sachs responded with an October rate hike call, reinforcing tightening fears across rate-sensitive assets. The Nasdaq advanced despite the monetary tightening on September 17, 2026.

stories.t: Globaltech Pursues Nasdaq Uplisting
stories.b: Globaltech seeks a Nasdaq uplisting after completing a reverse 1-for-3 split and planning governance changes. Nasdaq has not approved this move yet because the company does not meet all listing requirements. Stock Titan reported on September 17, 2026, that the corporation still lacks approval.
stories.i: Globaltech seeks a Nasdaq uplisting after executing a reverse 1-for-3 split and outlining governance changes. Nasdaq has not approved the move because the company does not yet meet listing requirements. Stock Titan noted the lack of approval on September 17, 2026.
stories.a: Globaltech pursued a Nasdaq uplisting following a reverse 1-for-3 split and intended governance overhauls. Nasdaq withheld approval as the issuer fails to satisfy baseline listing requirements as of September 17, 2026.

politics.b: President Trump claimed the Federal Reserve is raising interest rates for political reasons.
politics.i: President Trump asserted that the Federal Reserve is raising interest rates for political motives.
politics.a: President Trump publicly alleged political motivations behind the Federal Reserve rate hikes.

United Kingdom.label: United Kingdom
United Kingdom.sub: Bank of England holds rates as inflation reaches 3.1%

stories.t: Interest Rates Held Steady at 3.75%
stories.b: The Bank of England keeps its main interest rate at 3.75%. An interest rate is like the cost of borrowing money. Officials voted 6-3 to leave the rate alone. Prices rose faster in August 2026. Consumer prices increased by 3.1% compared to the previous year.
stories.i: The Bank of England maintained its benchmark rate at 3.75% following a 6-3 split vote among policymakers. This decision occurred as inflation reached a five-month high of 3.1% in August 2026. Officials flagged ongoing pressures from energy costs in their latest announcements.
stories.a: The Monetary Policy Committee preserved the Bank Rate at 3.75% via a 6-3 division amidst headline inflation printing at 3.1% for August 2026. Forward guidance emphasized persistent energy sector risks, complicating the policy trajectory relative to global peers.

stories.t: Bank of England Alters Asset Purchase Facility Plan
stories.b: The Bank of England changed how it handles past quantitative easing. Quantitative easing is when a central bank buys bonds to pump money into the economy. Officials announced plans to unwind the Asset Purchase Facility. The bank stopped selling long-dated versions of government debt known as gilts.
stories.i: The Bank of England updated its long-term strategy for dismantling quantitative easing through the Asset Purchase Facility. HM Treasury and the central bank exchanged letters on 17 September 2026 detailing these adjustments. Authorities halted sales of long-dated gilts as part of the operational shift.
stories.a: The central bank revised the quantitative easing unwind timeline for the Asset Purchase Facility via an exchange of letters with HM Treasury on 17 September 2026. Policymakers suspended sales of long-dated gilts, altering the quantitative tightening vector. This adjustment reconfigures balance sheet reduction mechanics without altering the benchmark policy rate.

politics.b: The Chancellor of the Exchequer and the Governor of the Bank of England exchanged official letters on 17 September 2026. These letters discussed inflation reaching 3.1% in August 2026. They also addressed updates to the Asset Purchase Facility.
politics.i: HM Treasury and the Bank of England published open letters on 17 September 2026 following August inflation figures of 3.1%. The Chancellor and the Governor corresponded directly regarding these economic indicators. They also announced structural updates to the Asset Purchase Facility.
politics.a: The Chancellor and the Governor formalised an exchange of correspondence on 17 September 2026 addressing the August CPI printing of 3.1%. These open letters coincided with operational announcements concerning the Asset Purchase Facility framework. HM Treasury sanctioned the updated parameters alongside the central bank.

timeline: The Bank of England held interest rates at 3.75% in a 6-3 split vote.
The Governor and the Chancellor exchanged open letters regarding August CPI inflation of 3.1%.
The Bank of England halted long-dated gilt sales as part of updates to the Asset Purchase Facility.

Germany.label: Germany
Germany.sub: DAX index climbs following rate decisions

stories.t: DAX climbs following central bank decisions
stories.b: The DAX is an index, which is a basket of big companies whose stock prices are tracked together to show how the stock market is doing. The DAX opened 0.77% higher following a rate decision by the US central bank. Hochtief stock gained as a DAX winner on a technical rebound. Bilfinger plunged during the session.
stories.i: The DAX opened 0.77% higher and reached an over one-week high following the US central bank rate decision. Hochtief stock advanced as a DAX winner on a technical rebound. Bilfinger shares plunged during the trading session.
stories.a: The DAX registered a 0.77% opening gain and pushed to an over one-week high in the wake of the Fed rate decision. Equity momentum favoured names like Hochtief on a technical rebound, while Bilfinger suffered a sharp plunge.

stories.t: German energy costs drive up consumer prices
stories.b: Inflation is when the cost of everyday things goes up over time, meaning your money buys less than it did before. German inflation rose to 2.9%. This increase happened as energy prices climbed.
stories.i: German inflation accelerated to 2.9%. Rising energy prices drove the headline consumer price increase.
stories.a: German inflation printed at 2.9%. The upward print was propelled by advancing energy costs across the economy.

politics.a: Quirino Governor Dax Cua passed away at 48 years of age.

Japan.label: Japan
Japan.sub: Bank of Japan rate path and US investment talks

stories.t: Bank of Japan Rate Move and Currency Pressures
stories.b: The Bank of Japan raised its interest rate to 1.25%. Interest is the cost of borrowing money. Central banks use these hikes to manage their economies. Despite this increase, the Japanese yen failed to gain strength because of US monetary policy. Traders now look closely at future guidance from Japanese officials.
stories.i: The Bank of Japan lifted its benchmark rate to 1.25%. This rate hike failed to support the Japanese yen due to broader Federal Reserve tightening. Global carry trades and currency pressures complicate domestic monetary policy. Analysts now focus on subsequent central bank guidance.
stories.a: The Bank of Japan advanced rates to 1.25%. Hawkish Federal Reserve adjustments undermined the efficacy of this tightening cycle on the Japanese yen. Second-order effects from US rate trajectories continue to impede domestic carry trade unwinding. Market participants now reprice terminal rate expectations contingent on incoming central bank guidance.

stories.t: Corporate Refinancing and Stablecoin Pilots
stories.b: Orix JREIT secured 10.6 billion yen in new loans to refinance existing debt. Refinancing means replacing old loans with new ones. Meanwhile, Kyobo Life Insurance and SBI completed a pilot for direct yen-won stablecoin exchanges without using the US dollar. Stablecoins are digital tokens pegged to traditional currencies.
stories.i: Orix JREIT secured 10.6 billion yen in new credit facilities to refinance debt obligations. Kyobo Life Insurance and SBI completed a pilot for direct yen-won stablecoin exchanges, bypassing the US dollar intermediary. These developments reflect ongoing capital management shifts across Japanese financial institutions.
stories.a: Orix JREIT secured 10.6 billion yen in new credit facilities to refinance maturing debt. Kyobo Life Insurance and SBI finalized a bilateral yen-won stablecoin settlement pilot, eliminating US dollar intermediation friction. These transactional rails modify traditional cross-border settlement mechanics.

politics.b: Japan and the United States are discussing chip factory construction as part of a larger 550 billion dollar investment package. Lawmakers and industry leaders are reviewing manufacturing capacity. Trade talks between the two nations continue.
politics.i: Japan and the United States are discussing chip factory construction as part of US$550 billion bilateral investment talks. Government officials and corporate representatives continue negotiating industrial collaboration. Semiconductor supply chain security remains a primary focus of these discussions.
politics.a: Japan and the United States are discussing semiconductor fabrication plant construction within the framework of US$550 billion investment talks. Bilateral delegations are structuring industrial subsidies and capital commitments. These negotiations target long-term technological integration between both jurisdictions.

India.label: India
India.sub: RBI bond auctions and rupeee movements

stories.t: Reserve Bank of India Sells Government Securities
stories.b: The central bank of a country manages money and banks. It sold government debt worth ₹50,000 crore through an auction. Financial institutions made total bids of ₹66,590 crore for these assets. The bank accepted all ₹50,000 crore of those offers.
stories.i: The Reserve Bank of India sold ₹50,000 crore of government securities via an open market operation. Total bids reached ₹66,590 crore across six different debt instruments maturing between 2009 and 2032. The institution accepted the full notified amount at yields ranging from 6.6007% to 7.0090%.
stories.a: The Reserve Bank of India absorbed liquidity by clearing ₹50,000 crore of sovereign paper across a six-security auction spanning the 2029 to 2032 maturity bracket. Aggregate demand reached ₹66,590 crore, allowing the central bank to fully allot the notified volume with cut-off yields spanning 6.6007% for the 7.59% GS 2029 up to 7.0090% for the 8.28% GS 2032.

stories.t: Central Bank Cancels and Surrenders NBFC Registrations
stories.b: The Reserve Bank of India took away licenses from five financial companies. Eight other finance firms decided to give back their business certificates voluntarily. The central bank used specific laws from 1934 to cancel these permissions.
stories.i: The Reserve Bank of India cancelled the registration certificates of five non-banking financial companies. Another eight financial entities voluntarily surrendered their operating permits. All cancellations utilized powers granted under Section 45-IA (6) of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
stories.a: The Reserve Bank of India revoked the certification of five non-banking financial companies under Section 45-IA (6) of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934. A separate group of eight non-banking financial companies formally surrendered their permits to exit the sector.

stories.t: Indian Equities and Currency Respond to Global Rates
stories.b: Stock markets in India stayed mostly flat after another country raised borrowing costs. The local currency dropped past 96 against the dollar before bouncing back. It finished the day down just 3 paise at 95.94.
stories.i: Indian stock benchmarks traded sideways following a rate increase by the United States Federal Reserve. The Nifty index closed above the 23,250 level while market focus centered on upcoming public share offerings. The domestic currency dropped below 96 before recovering to settle 3 paise lower at 95.94.
stories.a: Indian equities hovered near flat trajectories as local benchmarks digested the latest Federal Reserve tightening cycle. The Nifty closed above 23,250 alongside steady institutional attention on the National Stock Exchange initial public offering pipeline. The rupee breached 95.94 after dipping below 96 during intraday sessions.

politics.b: The central bank conducted government debt sales and altered financial company registrations.
politics.i: The Reserve Bank of India adjusted liquidity via open market operations and reshuffled non-banking financial company licenses.
politics.a: Regulatory interventions encompassed open market operations totaling ₹50,000 crore alongside statutory cancellations of non-banking financial company registrations under the Reserve Bank of India Act.

timeline: The extant scheme of underwriting commitment was notified.
The Reserve Bank of India held an open market sale auction for government securities.
The settlement for the open market operation sale auction took place.

Brazil.label: Brazil
Brazil.sub: Petrobras deals and central bank rate cuts

stories.t: Petrobras Contracts and Software Agreements
stories.b: Vallourec secures a pipe deal for a Petrobras project in the pre-salt area. Computer Modelling Group and Petrobras renew a simulation software agreement over multiple years. Mol and Petrobras sign a long-term deal for a cargo transfer vessel. Strohm wins a deepwater TCP contract offshore Brazil from Petrobras.
stories.i: Vallourec secures a pipe contract for a Petrobras pre-salt project. Computer Modelling Group and Petrobras renew a multi-year simulation software agreement. Mol and Petrobras finalise a long-term deal for a cargo transfer vessel. Strohm receives a deepwater TCP contract offshore Brazil from Petrobras.
stories.a: Vallourec captures a pipe supply agreement for a Petrobras pre-salt development. Computer Modelling Group extends its multi-year simulation software pact with Petrobras. Mol executes a long-term agreement with Petrobras for a cargo transfer vessel. Strohm secures a deepwater TCP contract offshore Brazil from Petrobras.

stories.t: Interest Rate Cuts and Diesel Subsidy Adjustments
stories.b: The Central Bank of Brazil cuts its benchmark interest rate, known as the Selic, down to 13.75%. This is the fifth straight reduction in borrowing costs. Petrobras raises average diesel prices to distributors by 1 real per litre. The government offsets this fuel increase with a new subsidy and discount program.
stories.i: The Central Bank of Brazil lowers the Selic rate to 13.75% in its fifth consecutive reduction. Petrobras increases average diesel prices to distributors by 1 real per litre. Petrobras simultaneously grants a discount in the exact same amount under a new diesel subsidy program.
stories.a: The Central Bank of Brazil reduces the Selic rate by cutting borrowing costs to 13.75% through its fifth successive easing move. Petrobras implements an average diesel price increase of 1 real per litre to distributors. Petrobras offsets the distribution price adjustment by granting an equivalent discount via a fiscal subsidy scheme.

politics.b: Petrobras adjusts diesel prices and grants equivalent discounts under a state subsidy program. The central bank lowers the Selic interest rate to 13.75% ahead of an election. Petrobras continues signing multiple offshore supply and software deals.
politics.i: Petrobras implements a diesel price increase matched by a state-backed subsidy discount. The Central Bank of Brazil reduces the Selic rate to 13.75% ahead of the upcoming election. Petrobras concurrently executes various operational and software vendor agreements.
politics.a: Petrobras manages domestic fuel pricing pressures via simultaneous price hikes and subsidy-funded distribution discounts. The Central Bank of Brazil implements its fifth consecutive rate reduction, bringing the Selic to 13.75% ahead of the election cycle. Petrobras simultaneously secures multiple deepwater infrastructure and software contracts.

timeline: Petrobras awards Strohm a deepwater TCP contract offshore Brazil.

Saudi Arabia.label: Saudi Arabia
Saudi Arabia.sub: Aramco oil supply halt and digital shutdown tool launch

stories.t: Aramco Stops Crude Supplies to Indian Refiners and Cancels European Cargoes
stories.b: Saudi Aramco stopped sending crude oil to Indian refiners after a pipeline was hit. The company also cancelled September oil cargoes destined for Europe. Oil prices surged above $105 per barrel following the supply disruptions and reported regional attacks. Houthis claimed missile and drone strikes on a Saudi air base and Aramco facilities.
stories.i: Saudi Aramco halted crude oil supplies to Indian refiners after a key pipeline was hit amid a Gulf crisis. The disruption expanded as the state producer cancelled European oil cargoes for September. Benchmark oil prices surged above $105 per barrel following these supply restrictions and reported Houthi missile and drone strikes on energy infrastructure.
stories.a: Saudi Aramco suspended crude deliveries to Indian buyers and rescinded September European crude allocations following kinetic impacts on critical midstream infrastructure. Brent-linked benchmarks breached $105 per barrel as physical tightness materialized concurrently with Houthi claims of drone and missile attacks targeting national air bases and processing facilities. The export curtailment forces refiners globally to bid aggressively for prompt replacement barrels in an already constrained spot market.

stories.t: Wipro and SAP Launch AI Plant Tool Following Aramco Tech Value Report
stories.b: Wipro collaborated with Aramco and SAP to launch the Wipro STO360 tool. The artificial intelligence tool helps companies manage plant shutdowns, turnarounds, and outages efficiently. Meanwhile, Aramco stated that technology delivered $5 billion in value last year.
stories.i: Wipro partnered with Aramco and SAP to introduce the Wipro STO360 solution. The artificial intelligence-powered platform helps industrial companies manage plant shutdowns, turnarounds, and outages. Separately, Aramco reported that digital technology deployment generated $5 billion in corporate value over the previous year.
stories.a: Wipro commercialized its STO360 enterprise solution in coordination with Aramco and SAP to automate complex facility turnarounds, shutdowns, and outages via machine learning algorithms. The release coincides with Aramco disclosing that proprietary digital transformation initiatives yielded $5 billion in enterprise value over the prior twelve months. This software integration targets operational expenditure optimization across heavy industrial asset bases.

politics.b: Yemeni Houthi leaders stated they launched missile and drone strikes targeting Aramco and a Saudi air base. The military claims followed regional tensions and attacks on key infrastructure.
politics.i: Houthi forces claimed responsibility for missile and drone strikes hitting Aramco facilities and a Saudi air base amid escalating regional hostilities.
politics.a: Attribution of strikes targeting national air bases and Aramco processing infrastructure was claimed by Houthi military spokespersons amid broader Gulf security friction.

timeline: Aramco reports technology delivered $5 billion in value during the prior year.
Wipro, Aramco, and SAP launch the STO360 tool for plant shutdown management.
Saudi Aramco halts crude oil supplies to Indian refiners and cancels European cargoes.

Nigeria.label: Nigeria
Nigeria.sub: Naira movements, bank earnings, and potential rate cuts

stories.t: Naira Fluctuates at Official Foreign Exchange Market
stories.src: Tribune Online · Business Post Nigeria · THISDAYLIVE
stories.b: The official foreign exchange market is where businesses and banks buy and sell different national currencies. The Nigerian currency, the naira, lost 56 kobo against the US dollar in recent trading. The naira also dropped in value during another official trading session. However, the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market recorded $2.63bn in turnover across five sessions.
stories.i: The official FX market recorded $2.63bn in turnover across five sessions while the naira weakened by 56 kobo against the dollar. The currency continued to depreciate in subsequent official trading sessions. These currency movements occur alongside broader discussions about foreign exchange reforms by the central bank.
stories.a: Volume across five sessions reached $2.63bn at the Nigerian Foreign Exchange Market while the spot rate showed the naira sliding 56 kobo against the US dollar. Subsequent official windows confirmed further depreciation against the greenback. Observers link ongoing liquidity shifts to broader monetary policy and structural foreign exchange reforms.

stories.t: Fitch Reports Foreign Earnings Boost for Nigerian Banks
stories.b: Credit rating agencies look at how healthy financial companies are. Fitch Ratings stated that past drops in the value of the naira helped Nigerian banks. Because the local currency fell, money earned by foreign subsidiaries became worth more when converted back home. This boosted the total earnings reported by those banks.
stories.i: Fitch Ratings reported that past currency depreciation boosted the foreign subsidiaries’ earnings contribution to Nigerian banks. Translating external revenues back into the domestic currency magnified those financial results. Such cross-border gains cushioned local lenders during domestic volatility.
stories.a: Fitch highlighted that historical naira devaluation structurally enhanced the earnings contribution from foreign subsidiaries to domestic banking groups. Translation effects from external operations generated outsized top-line growth when reported in local currency terms. This geographical diversification acted as a key hedge against domestic operational headwinds.

stories.t: Analysts Anticipate Interest Rate Cuts Amid Softening Prices
stories.b: Interest rates are the cost of borrowing money, set by central banks to control price increases. Observers in financial markets predict that Nigeria might soon lower its borrowing costs. This expectation comes because consumer price pressures are softening and the naira has shown periods of strength. Lower rates make loans cheaper for businesses and consumers.
stories.i: Market participants project that the central bank will cut interest rates in response to softer inflation readings. A stronger naira and cooling price pressures provide monetary authorities room to ease policy. Lower rates typically encourage domestic borrowing and capital investment.
stories.a: Consensus expectations point toward monetary easing as incoming data shows moderating headline inflation prints. Improved currency stability gives the central bank room to pivot away from tight policy settings. Traders are pricing in a shift toward a lower benchmark rate trajectory.

politics.b: Labour unions demanded wage awards and requested that local refineries receive crude oil priced in naira to help lower petrol prices. The Nigeria Labour Council pressed authorities for interventions to protect workers from high living costs. Officials continue to face pressure over fuel pricing and domestic economic policies.
politics.i: The Nigeria Labour Congress demanded wage awards alongside the allocation of crude oil priced in naira to local refineries. These proposals aim to curb escalating petrol prices and ease cost-of-living pressures on workers. Labor groups continue to press state and federal authorities for direct market interventions.
politics.a: The Nigeria Labour Congress pushed demands for worker wage awards and mandated naira-denominated crude supplies for domestic refineries. These policy interventions target downstream petroleum pricing and domestic purchasing power erosion. Stakeholders continue to debate state-backed mechanisms to manage energy costs.

timeline: The official exchange rate for the dollar against the naira was recorded.
Fitch reported that naira devaluation boosted foreign subsidiary earnings for banks.

Australia.label: Australia

stories.t: Power Minerals Advances Brazilian Rare Earth Drilling
stories.b: Power Minerals, which trades on the Australian stock exchange under the code PNN, is moving forward with its rare earth drilling project in Brazil. Rare earth elements are a group of metals used in modern electronics. The company is advancing its operational plans at the site. The announcement was made on September 17, 2026. Power Minerals continues its exploration work in Brazil.
stories.i: Power Minerals (ASX:PNN) is advancing its rare earth drilling operations in Brazil. The company released operational updates regarding its exploration assets on September 17, 2026. Resource companies continue to develop overseas mineral projects to secure critical raw material supplies. Power Minerals maintains its drilling schedule at the Brazilian project site. Exploration activities at the rare earth prospect remain ongoing.
stories.a: Power Minerals (ASX:PNN) progresses its Brazilian rare earth drilling campaign, maintaining momentum across its foreign exploration assets. The firm issued project updates on September 17, 2026, detailing operational advancements at the target site. This development reflects broader industry efforts to expand alternative mineral supply chains outside traditional domestic jurisdictions. Drilling operations at the Brazilian prospect proceed according to the updated schedule. Power Minerals reports ongoing technical progress at the rare earth property.

stories.t: EQ Resources Enters US Tungsten Processing Joint Venture
stories.b: EQ Resources, with the stock code EQR, has joined a new business partnership in the United States. A joint venture is a business arrangement where two or more companies share a project. This partnership focuses on processing tungsten, which is a hard and rare metal. The announcement was published on September 17, 2026. EQ Resources is expanding its operations into the American market.
stories.i: EQ Resources (ASX:EQR) has entered a joint venture focused on tungsten processing in the United States. The company announced the new partnership on September 17, 2026. This arrangement establishes a commercial footprint in the North American critical minerals sector. Processing facilities will handle tungsten materials under the terms of the joint venture. EQ Resources expands its international operating portfolio through this agreement.
stories.a: EQ Resources (ASX:EQR) finalises a United States joint venture targeting domestic tungsten processing capabilities. The firm disclosed the partnership structure on September 17, 2026, securing an operational bridge into the North American critical minerals processing market. The agreement leverages regional processing assets to handle feedstock materials. EQ Resources executes its international expansion strategy via this venture. Operational integration of the US processing facilities proceeds under the agreed terms.
